open_points.subject: A18 backup inclusion of transactions committed during a copy
open_points.text: “a change committed while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the next” conflicts with “the days this rule and rule 5 leave without a kept backup are allowed,” failed runs, and later transactions that may erase or supersede that change before the next snapshot.
open_points.question: What does “is in the next” mean when the next run is missed or fails, or when a later transaction removes or supersedes the committed state before the next backup snapshot?
options: The next attempted run must contain the change even if the run keeps no backup.
The next successfully kept backup must preserve the change even if later transactions removed or superseded it.
A later backup contains only the state visible at its own snapshot, so the change is not guaranteed to appear in any backup.
open_points.default_guess: Treat each backup solely as its own snapshot: the next kept backup contains the committed change only if its effects still exist when that snapshot begins.

witness.initial: A daily backup copy is in progress, and no later kept backup yet exists.
events: The owner commits a project correction while the copy is being made.
The owner commits another correction restoring the old values before the next backup run.
The next daily run succeeds and takes its snapshot after both corrections.
outcomes: The new sentence requires the first correction to be in the next backup.
The one-snapshot rule requires the next backup to contain only the state after the second correction, with no preserved first-correction state except any audit entry that still remains.
witness.observer: The owner restoring or inspecting the next kept backup sees whether the intermediate committed state was preserved.
